intro: A snapshot of what's shipped, what's in flight, and what's on the map. Subject to change as we learn what teams actually need.
canonicalOrderNote: This roadmap is the canonical order — the labelled phase tags inside the admin menu (the muted 'Phase 1.X' pills on future tiles) reference these same numbers. When the order changes, this file moves first.

sections.title: Shipped
sections.summary: The current release stream covers the foundations.

items.title: Single binary deploy
items.description: Go server with the SvelteKit SPA embedded via `go:embed`. Multi-arch Docker images (amd64 + arm64), `.deb` + `.rpm` packages with systemd unit, static binaries for linux / macOS / Windows, Homebrew formula. Every image Sigstore-signed.

items.title: Postgres + storage
items.description: Goose migrations run on boot. Storage backend is filesystem by default, or any S3-compatible bucket (AWS, R2, B2, MinIO).

items.title: Identity, teams, audit
items.description: Full admin identity surface: paginated user list with search + status filter, user lifecycle states (pending / approved / disabled) with the `users.approve` capability split out for a future User Approver role, multi-device session management + revoke + 'current session' marker, password change + admin reset + bcrypt reuse-history (Phase 1.17.D), teams admin UI on the existing handlers (1.17.E), per-user capability grants + revokes (1.17.F), per-asset-type ACLs (1.17.F-bis), and the admin audit-log viewer with filter facets + per-event changeset rendering (1.17.K). Server-side: `auth.Identity.Can()` consults capability ↔ license-feature mappings BEFORE the SuperAdmin shortcut so install-level licensing trumps any per-user RBAC grant. See [ADR 0010](/adr/0010-permissions-teams-workflow/).

items.title: Licensing + enterprise gates
items.description: Ed25519 license verifier with embedded publisher key catalog + admin `/admin/system/license` status surface + paste-in upload UI with code-keyed i18n for every verifier error (1.17.O-1/2). Layer-1 cross-binding via customer-held `org.key` seed verified against the license's `org_pubkey` claim at boot + on every upload + on a 24h re-verify ticker (1.17.O-3) — a stolen `.lic` alone is useless without the matching key. `auth.IdentityProvider` interface + license-gated `Registry` so `ldapauth` / `samlauth` / `tenancy` enterprise stubs refuse to register without their feature flag and detach hot when a license downgrades (1.17.P-foundation). Hot-swap: `Registry.Replace` + `State.OnReload` callback so Community → Enterprise upgrades activate without a process restart. Federation is deliberately **not** gated (per design, small communities self-organize freely). See [ADR 0017 § Status](/adr/0017-monetization-and-licensing/).

items.title: Upload pipeline
items.description: Drag-anywhere → modal queue → background uploads with progress, per-row tags + per-asset metadata, three post-composition modes (one post / one-per-file / no-post), separate-cover-thumbnail support.

items.title: Posts + assets + collections
items.description: Posts wrap one or many assets; collections wrap posts; tags + full-text search across all of it.

items.title: Browse feed
items.description: Grid / masonry / thumbnail / list views with the sortable spreadsheet for list mode (toggleable columns, per-row thumbnails). Floating footer with view + feed filter (team / trending / latest / following) + sort direction.

items.title: Post detail modal
items.description: Two-pane shell, multi-asset vertical scroller, sidebar with per-asset metadata, comments thread, likes, dedicated review canvas with zoom / pan / tile.

items.title: Admin shell
items.description: 13-section admin menu with dynamic landing pages, capability-gated; Scalar-embedded API explorer; real config surfaces for site, SMTP, auth providers, AI providers, appearance (font slot picker — 14 fonts across 4 slots).

items.title: Account shell
items.description: Profile, theme + language preferences, API tokens management. Other surfaces (security, sessions, drafts, trash, activity, stats) stubbed with phase tags.

items.title: Theme system
items.description: M3-shaped color tokens (3-tier surface ladder, semantic success/warning/danger, on-* pairs, focus ring), light + dark palettes with intentional cross-mode hue shift, admin-configurable font slots (brand / display / sans / mono).

items.title: i18n
items.description: Per-user language preference, locale catalogue endpoint, hand-rolled flat-key dictionary store; English shipped, Spanish + French stubs for the picker.

items.title: Universal asset viewer
items.description: A single Svelte shell hosts per-kind view bodies (image, video, audio, PDF, font, 3D) with a shared anchor model — frame for video, page for PDF, camera + time-on-track for 3D — so future annotation overlays and presentation rooms wire to the shell once and every kind inherits them. Universal pan + zoom (⌘-wheel zoom-toward-cursor), click-to-pause, fullscreen + `F`, jump-to-frame (`G`), and per-kind transport bars all sit on the shell. Phase 1.18.B-2 + 1.18.E-6.

items.title: Format coverage
items.description: Images: PNG, JPEG, WebP, plus HDR / EXR / Radiance `.pic` via ffmpeg tonemap and a pure-Go RGBE decoder. Video: HLS adaptive ladder with frame-accurate scrubbing. Audio: waveform PNG + click-to-seek scrub. PDF: multi-page navigator + raster. Fonts: specimen render with interactive Try-it. 3D: native viewers for glTF / GLB / OBJ / FBX / Marmoset `.mview`, Blender-rendered turntable thumbnails for heavy formats, pure-Go importers for legacy game formats (MD2 / MD3 / MDL / MS3D). Ebooks: in-app EPUB reader with typography + scroll memory. Comics: cover-extraction thumbnails for CBZ / CBR / CB7. Audiobooks: m4b chapter probe with `.nfo` / `.cue` companion fold and multi-file playlist auto-advance. Archives: zip / tar / 7z / rar / tar.xz browser with in-place file tree + CodeMirror-syntax-highlighted entry preview + Extract-all bundle. Docs: CodeMirror 6 reader for text/code with syntax highlighting + text-range annotations (highlight / strike / underline / comment / note) + lint-style diagnostics. Sprite sheets: auto-detect + per-frame tools + onion-skin + export. Asset companion files (textures, `.mtl`, `.bin`) resolved per-asset. Phase 1.18.A / 1.18.B-1 / 1.18.B-10 / 1.18.B-12 / 1.18.B-15 / 1.18.C / 1.18.D / 1.18.E.

items.title: Whiteboard / brush surface
items.description: Post-anchored brush canvas with pen / marker / highlighter / eraser, stamp-based brush renderer (built-in soft + hard round) + ABR (Adobe Photoshop Brush) parser with owner-scoped pack upload + storage. MS-Paint-style sectioned sidebar with shapes (rect / ellipse / triangle / line / arrow + nine more), text with Google Fonts, custom HSL+RGB+Hex+Eyedropper color picker, Color 1 / Color 2 split, shape outline + fill, image transforms, rect-select + lasso + Select All + Invert + crop, copy / cut / paste, layers, infinite canvas with pan + zoom-toward-cursor + minimap. Element-typed model (strokes / shapes / text / images / connectors with auto-reroute / frames / sticky notes / mindmap nodes) with element comments as the annotation foundation.

sections.title: In flight
sections.summary: These have foundations in place; the rest of the surface area is the current focus.

items.title: First tagged release
items.description: `v0.1.0` against the channels above. Pre-1.0 means schemas can still break across minors.

items.title: Image processing pipeline
items.description: Variant generation (col / preview / screen / hires), thumbhash placeholders, content-addressed cache headers, generic background-job queue with in-process workers + HTTP claim API for external farms / federated peers.

items.title: Video pipeline + animator review player
items.description: The load-bearing UX: a SyncSketch / Keyframe-Pro-2 replacement built into the post modal. See 'Review tool' arc below for the full feature plan.

items.title: AI auto-tagging
items.description: Use the configured AI providers for tag inference on upload + reverse-image search via embeddings. Provider list is open: cloud-API providers (OpenAI / Anthropic / Google) plus **locally-installed capability add-ons** (Phase 1.42) — CLIP for embeddings, custom classifiers for studio-specific taxonomies. Operator picks the active provider per slot; the runtime resolves through the precedence chain (local add-on → cloud-bridge add-on → external cloud).

sections.title: Review tool — the load-bearing UX arc
sections.summary: The post modal is becoming the animator's review tool. Phase 1.18.B ships in sub-phases so each piece can be tested against real review sessions before the next lands.

subphases.title: Video pipeline
bullets: ffmpeg-based preview.video handler: probe → poster → HLS adaptive ladder (480p / 720p / 1080p) → 100-cell sprite sheet + WebVTT.
Encoder detection at boot: probes ffmpeg `-encoders` AND verifies each candidate with a 4-frame synthetic encode. Picks NVENC > QSV > VideoToolbox > libx264. Falls back gracefully on any failure.
Wildcard chi route for multi-segment HLS variant keys.

`<video>` element with HLS.js (native HLS on Safari). HUD with HH:MM:SS:FF timecode + frame counter via `requestVideoFrameCallback`. JKL transport, ±1 / ±10 frame step (arrows + comma/period + Shift), I/O loop region, 1-5 speed presets, sticky muted-autoplay + persistent volume via localStorage, sprite hover preview on the scrubber.
Mounted in the post carousel directly (no extra Review-mode click).

subphases.title: Player polish + quality-of-life
bullets: Click-to-pause on the video canvas; click-and-drag scrub on the HUD timecode.
Fullscreen button + `F` shortcut; always-on-top (PiP) when the browser allows.
Jump-to-frame input + jump-to-timecode parser.
Pan + zoom on the video frame (mouse wheel + drag) — pixel-perfect inspection without leaving playback.
Flip + rotate (H / V / 90°).
Ping-pong loop, hold-frame at IN/OUT, range bookmarks.
Frame bookmarks (single + range) with cycle hotkeys.
Audio scrub (variable-speed) while dragging the playhead.
Screen capture to clipboard / file.

subphases.title: Subtitle viewer integration
bullets: Native WebVTT `<track>` element attachment for every `final` caption track on the asset (one per language).
Track picker in the player chrome — language label + kind badge (`captions` / `subtitles` / `descriptions`).
Per-user subtitle preferences (default language, font size, position, background opacity); persisted on the account row.
Auto-attach also on the share-link viewer (ADR 0018) and the public-portal embed.
Caption track production, editing, translation, and download bundling — including the Whisper auto-transcribe loop — live in Phase 1.44 (ADR 0037). This subphase is the viewer-side consumer only.

subphases.title: Image sequences + RAM cache + always-on-top
bullets: Treat an image-sequence asset (numbered PNG/EXR/JPEG run) as a first-class playable timeline.
Client-side RAM cache: pre-decoded frame buffer for instant scrub on short clips.
'Always on top' window mode (browser PiP / SPA detached window).

subphases.title: Presentation rooms (global, real-time)
bullets: Presentation is a global capability — image, video, 3D, PDF, any asset that can be shown. The player / viewer is a host; the 'presentation room' is a separate concern that wraps any host.
WebSocket presence room keyed on `(post_id or asset_id)`: live cursor, live scrub position, who's watching.
Synchronous mode: a presenter drives the playhead / camera / page. Observers follow. Offline = solo (default).
Shared chat + reactions alongside whatever's being shown.
Mobile + tablet observers via the same UI.
The protocol is asset-type-agnostic: a frame number, a 3D camera matrix, a PDF page index — all 'anchor' objects the host sends on each tick. Observers' viewers replay them.

subphases.title: Annotation system (global, frame/anchor-aware)
bullets: Annotations are a global capability too — they live in their own package and any asset host (image, video, 3D, PDF) surfaces them.

Anchor model: an annotation binds to an asset_id PLUS an asset-type-specific anchor — a frame number for video, a camera+target for 3D, a page+x/y for PDF, a coord+zoom for images. The same `annotations` table stores them all; the host package owns rendering.
Brush engine: pen, highlighter, eraser, shapes, text, arrows. Clean-room Svelte implementation.
Foreground + background layers; background transparency.
Laser pointer for live review (broadcasts via the presentation room when one is active).
Ghosting / onion-skin between adjacent anchors (video frames, 3D camera takes, PDF pages).
Annotation bookmarks; cycle hotkeys.
PDF page annotations: anchored to `(asset_id, page, x, y, w, h)`; rendered against the PDF raster preview.
PDF summary export with comment thread + screenshots per anchor.

subphases.title: Timeline assembly
bullets: Build a review timeline from multiple source files (different takes, different shots).
Per-source in / out points, ordering, audio override.
Seamless playback between sources.
Export the assembled timeline as a standalone media file (ffmpeg).

subphases.title: A/B comparison
bullets: Split viewer (horizontal / vertical / grid).
A/B wipe with draggable seam.
A/B transparency / overlay blend.
Pair any two assets — different versions, reference footage.

subphases.title: DCC integrations
bullets: Python client API for external tools to drive the player (open, seek, annotate, snapshot).
Maya → review send-back script.
Blender / Houdini integrations (community-driven via the same API).
Webhook + presence broadcasts for studio production trackers.

subphases.title: 3D viewer (native)
bullets: `<model-viewer>` for glTF / GLB native — instant load, AR, animations.
three.js loader fallbacks for OBJ (+ .mtl + texture set) and FBX.
Marmoset Toolbag `.mview` native player (self-contained JS).
USDZ via Quick Look on Apple devices.
Camera presets, lighting picker, turntable poster generation, wireframe / UV inspect modes.

subphases.title: 3D heavy converters (worker side)
bullets: Blender headless → glTF for `.blend`.
FBX2glTF for cached glTF when the source format is heavy.
Maya `.mb` / `.ma` and 3ds Max `.max` — extract embedded preview where possible; full conversion gated on a licensed converter side-car. Native-viewer-first; convert only on miss.
Per-format converter run as a separate job type so a render farm can pick it up.

subphases.title: Audio / SVG / PDF / fonts
bullets: Audio waveform PNG + scrub.
SVG → rasterized variant set.
PDF first-page raster + multi-page navigator.
Font specimen render.

subphases.title: Project / workspace
bullets: 'Review project' entity: a collection of assets curated for a review session, with timelines, annotations, chat history.
Save / share / fork projects.
Snapshot a project state for 'this is what we showed at the Tuesday review'.

subphases.title: Federation + share-with-anyone
bullets: Public share link with permission scope (view / comment / annotate) and optional expiry.
Federated peer instances surface annotations + chat back to the origin instance. The job queue's existing `origin_server_id` + the HTTP claim API are the carrier.
Quick-generate PDF summary for offline clients.

subphases.title: Sprite-sheet viewer
bullets: Auto-slice by uniform grid (rows × cols, configurable cell size) and by edge-detection (find tightest bounding box per visible region) — operator picks the strategy per asset.
Frame index panel with thumbnails; reorder, name, and group frames into named action sequences (idle / walk / attack).
Animation timeline + scrubber that plays the slices in order with configurable FPS, ping-pong, hold-frame, and onion-skin between adjacent frames. Reuses the existing video HUD primitives.

Per-frame metadata persisted as a sidecar companion JSON (action ranges, per-frame notes, slices, alt-files). Anchor-tagged annotation integration with 1.18.B-6 deferred — the companion format is forward-compatible.
Export individual cels as PNG / WebP, or export the action set as a packed sprite sheet (PNG + JSON) or a per-frame zip; client-side GIF export via gifenc.

subphases.title: Texture inspector
bullets: Channel splitter: view R / G / B / A as separate greyscale views, or as a packed-channel overlay (e.g., R = roughness, G = metallic, B = ambient occlusion — the convention surfaces in the inspector UI so reviewers don't have to guess).
Linear ↔ sRGB toggle for accurate color-managed review of source textures vs runtime appearance.
Normal map preview with light-source rotation; tangent-space validation (is this normal map decoded the way you think it is?).
Mip-chain preview: scroll through pre-computed mip levels at the size they'll appear in-engine. Catch mip-popping problems before ship.
Alpha channel mode: solid / checkerboard / outline overlay so reviewers can see transparency cleanly.
File-format awareness: BC1 / BC3 / BC5 / BC7 / ASTC / ETC2 decoders so the inspector shows what the engine actually sees, not just what Photoshop saved.

subphases.title: Color & palette inspector
bullets: Eyedropper with hex / RGB / HSL / OKLCH readout; copy to clipboard in any format.
Dominant-color extraction: top-N palette of any image, with share-of-pixels percentages. Useful for 'does this character match our style palette?' reviews.
Palette comparison: drop two assets side by side, see their extracted palettes overlaid, with delta-E coverage of every swatch. Catches style drift between artists.
Save and name reference palettes per workflow / collection; validate any new upload against a reference palette and warn on drift beyond a configurable delta-E threshold.

subphases.title: Bitmap / format inspector
bullets: Size diff between source and encoded variants: source PNG vs BC3 vs BC7 vs ASTC, byte-for-byte and as a percentage. Helps optimization reviewers spot regressions.
Side-by-side encoded preview against the source, with the same A/B wipe primitives from 1.18.B-8 so format compression artifacts surface visually.
Alpha-on-color delta view: highlight pixels whose alpha or color changed between source and encoded variant, in any user-selectable color. Surfaces premultiply / unpremultiply mistakes immediately.
Per-format metadata badges: compression type, block size, encoder used, expected runtime cost. Operators know exactly what they're looking at without reading file headers manually.

architectureNote.title: How the global systems connect
paragraphs: The three layers stay separate so each evolves independently:
1. **Host viewers** — `ImageReview`, `VideoPlayer`, `ModelViewer`, `PDFViewer`, etc. Each owns its surface (pan/zoom, scrub, camera, page). All emit + accept a typed 'anchor' describing where we are.

2. **Annotation overlay** — a single Svelte component layered on top of any host. Reads + writes anchor-tagged annotations via the shared `/assets/{id}/annotations` API. Doesn't know about the host beyond the anchor schema.

3. **Presentation room** — a separate WebSocket-backed store that broadcasts the current anchor + cursor + chat. Any host can listen to it (slave its anchor to the presenter) and emit to it (when this user is the presenter).

Concretely: VideoPlayer emits `{type:"video", frame:N}` anchors; ModelViewer emits `{type:"model", camera:[...], target:[...]}`; PDFViewer emits `{type:"pdf", page:N, x, y, zoom}`. Annotations are indexed by `(asset_id, anchor_hash)`. Presentation rooms forward whatever anchor the presenter emits to everyone in the room.

sections.title: Up next
sections.summary: The phases queued behind the current focus.

items.title: Pre-MVP cleanup — shim drop, migration baseline, name sanitization
items.description: Foundational debt-clearing sweep landing between Phase 1.22.C (Share access control) and Phase 1.22.D (federation outbox). Three workstreams in one `chore/pre-mvp-cleanup` branch. **1.49.A — Drop the 7-shim panic-stub pattern.** Replace per-package OpenAPI test shims (~1,155 panic stubs across 7 files) with a single shared `internal/openapi/strictservershim.PanicShim`. Domain tests embed the shim and override only the methods they exercise; new OpenAPI operations stop requiring stub creation. **1.49.B — Drop legacy fallback paths in wired handlers.** Every handler currently has two code paths — gold-standard `WithEmission`/`WithEmissionFn` (writes domain row + activity ledger in one tx) and a legacy fallback (just the domain row). The fallback is a real federation-delivery correctness bug once 1.22.D outbox ships. Test fixtures get wired to the gold-standard path; the fallback is deleted. **1.49.C — DB migration baseline.** Per ADR 0046, audit the ~60-migration sequence for orphan tables / columns / redundant indexes / naming inconsistencies (`*_id` UUID vs `*_ref` BIGINT mixed). Audit report at `docs/cleanup-audit-<date>.md` ships in its own commit before the destructive squash. Then `pg_dump`-derived `00001_baseline_v1.sql` replaces the prior sequence; old migration files deleted outright (git preserves history); `app/schema.sql` mirror updated; sqlc regenerated. No upgrade path from the old sequence — developers `docker compose down -v` after pulling. **Pre-v1.0 only**; post-v1.0 migrations are append-only forever. **1.49.D — Product-name sanitization.** Strip direct competitor / inspiration references from source (Go, Svelte, SQL comments, OpenAPI). Reference files, ADR historical notes, and `docs/research/` retain the comparison framing — source code stays neutral per the new coding-standards rule. See ADR 0046 + the coding-standards developer doc.

items.title: Identity & teams — remaining extensions
items.description: Core Phase 1.17 identity surface is shipped (see the Shipped section). The remaining pieces from the original epic move to the next branch: resource-request workflow (user asks → capability-holder approves → notification fires → lifecycle tracked + auto-expiry), table-level audit changeset enrichment for the RS-parity items, and the real LDAP / SAML / OIDC bind/search/assertion impls that plug into the existing `auth.IdentityProvider` registry slots.

items.title: Audit log & change tracking
items.description: The central event log consolidating the audit-trail story currently scattered across Phases 1.17 / 1.20 / 1.21 / 1.24 / 1.26-1.28 / 1.32. Owns the event schema (actor + action + target + outcome + changeset before/after + metadata + correlation_id + license_kid), the dotted event taxonomy (`auth.*` / `user.*` / `asset.*` / `share.*` / `commerce.*` / `platform.*` / `system.*` / etc.), the capture API (`audit.Record(ctx, ...)` with buffered async writes — failure to record never fails the originating operation), the admin filter + search + detail + export surface at `/admin/audit`, retention policy (default 7 years, per-category overrides at Enterprise, enforced via the Phase 1.28 scheduled-action engine), and signed Enterprise export (Ed25519 over the JSONL payload, public key at `/.well-known/audit-signing-key` per ADR 0017). The `correlation_id` field links every event from a single request / job so cascade effects are reconstructable. Same features at Community + Pro; Enterprise adds the signed export, per-category retention overrides, and multi-instance audit-log federation. See ADR 0032.

items.title: Observability & operator telemetry
items.description: Production-readiness layer: `/metrics` Prometheus endpoint with HTTP / DB / job-queue / storage / cache / session / license / federation / audit families; OpenTelemetry tracing via OTLP with auto-instrumented HTTP / DB / job / external-API spans (10% sampling default, errors 100%, W3C Trace Context propagation); structured-log shipping via opt-in forwarder providers (Loki / Datadog / Cloudwatch / Vector / Promtail / syslog); per-subsystem log levels hot-reloaded from admin + a `?log_level=debug` per-request escape hatch; admin live-tail log viewer at `/admin/logs/tail` via WebSocket; pre-baked Grafana dashboards in `infra/grafana/dashboards/` for HTTP / job queue / storage / federation / license / audit. Health endpoints stay at `/healthz` + `/readyz` with detailed per-subsystem status at `/admin/system/health`. Same features at Community + Pro; Enterprise adds priority ops support, vendor-specific OTLP exporter configs (New Relic / Honeycomb / etc.), and an SLA on production incident resolution. See ADR 0033.

items.title: Capability add-ons — registry + installer
items.description: Out-of-band heavy components (CLIP / Whisper / Tesseract / Stable Diffusion / ComfyUI / Flux / future ML runtimes) ship as first-party add-ons pulled from a curated registry at `add-ons.artist-alley.org` — NOT baked into the binary. Sits between integrations (in-process Go) and future plugins (WASM): add-ons are heavy artefacts (Docker containers + model weights), optional, lifecycle-managed from a `/admin/capabilities` surface. Capability-slot model formalises the existing provider abstractions (image-embedding, transcription, OCR, image-classification, image-generation, image-inpaint, NSFW classification); multiple add-ons can satisfy a slot; operator picks the active provider. **No GPU gating** — operator hardware is operator hardware regardless of license tier; cloud-bridged add-ons (we host the inference) are the only tier-gated mode. Plugin-style YAML manifest format.Digest-verified pulls; air-gapped operators mirror the registry. Resource requirements are advisory, not enforcing. Audit hooks fire `addon.*` into Phase 1.40; metrics expose under `addon_` prefix in Phase 1.41. Phase 1.42 ships the registry + installer + first three add-ons (CLIP for image embeddings, Whisper for transcription, Tesseract for OCR) so the surface is meaningful at v1. See ADR 0034.

items.title: Integrations
items.description: Real LDAP / SAML / OAuth login flows, OAuth applications surface, outbound webhooks, notification rules + delivery channels. Extended with: email template engine + send queue with operator-editable templates, timezone-aware delivery (digest at 8 AM in the recipient's TZ), event-scoped notifications that link to a triggering record and auto-resolve when it resolves, conditional download terms (per-resource terms page based on metadata), and a dedicated webhook delivery worker — outbound webhooks are queued through the existing job system with exponential-backoff retries, per-endpoint signing secrets, delivery-log admin surface for inspection + manual re-send, dead-letter handling after N failures, and a `webhook.*` audit category (Phase 1.40). Chat platforms (Phase 1.30) plug in as one of the delivery channels.

items.title: Search 2.0
items.description: Advanced search builder with field-level filters, saved searches, smart collections, synonyms + boosts, search analytics. Extended with: saved-search alerts (notify when results change), endless scrolling in result views, categorical / faceted refinement with suggested-keyword refinements derived from the result set, customizable keyboard shortcuts for power-user tagging and review.

items.title: Licensing & monetization — wider derivation
items.description: The verifier core, admin upload UI, capability-layer gate, cross-binding, and enterprise-provider registry shipped early as Phase 1.17.O/P-foundation (see Shipped). Cloudflare signing service + customer portal live in the sibling `artist-alley-license-server` repo and are deployed. **Still planned:** the wider tangled-value derivation across non-capability consumers — `searchQuota`, `uploadConcurrency`, `cacheSize`, `thumbnailMaxRes`, `enabledPlugins`, `federationEnabled` — so stripping the verifier produces an obviously-broken install rather than just a misconfigured one. Lands per-subsystem as those code paths get touched. See [ADR 0016](/adr/0016-license-direction/) + [ADR 0017](/adr/0017-monetization-and-licensing/).

sections.title: On the map
sections.summary: Larger arcs that will land but aren't the current focus.

items.title: Privacy & consent management
items.description: Cookie / tracker banner that renders ONLY when a non-essential category is in use on the current instance (a bare studio install with no analytics shows no banner at all). Categories: essential, functional, analytics, third-party embeds. Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) tooling: machine-readable JSON export of all personal data, soft-then-hard deletion via the scheduled-action engine, reassignment of authored content to a `deleted-user` tombstone so collaborative content survives. Per-resource-type retention policies executed via the same scheduled-action engine. Editable `/legal/privacy` and `/legal/terms` markdown surfaces with a usable starting template (not legal advice). Privacy is not a paid differentiator — Community and Pro both get every feature; Enterprise adds non-repudiation signing on the audit-log export. See ADR 0024.

items.title: Share links
items.description: Signed, expiring resource + collection + post share URLs for external collaborators (contractors, publishers, agencies, festival juries) who do not have accounts. `GET /share/{token}` with the token as a 32-byte random ID and the share-link row as the source of truth — no HMAC signing, so revocation is single-click. Each link binds a target (asset / post / collection), a scope (`view` / `comment` / `annotate` / `download`), optional `nbf` / `exp`, optional Argon2id password, optional max-use ceiling. Per-fetch audit trail records IP + user-agent + password result + scope satisfied. Downloads stream via presigned URLs on S3-style backends. See ADR 0018.

items.title: Bulk operations
items.description: Multi-select edit / tag / delete / move-to-collection / state-transition across browse + search results. Floating action bar with persistent selection across pagination + `select all in filter` expansion. Destructive actions show preview counts and require typed-count confirmation. CSV export of search results with operator-picked columns. Contact-sheet PDF generation with configurable grid + per-thumb metadata footer. All bulk actions submit as a single job-queue job (cancellable, resumable, progress streamed) with audit entries preserving selection IDs for batch undo where reversible. See ADR 0019.

items.title: Asset gating & NDA workflow
items.description: Per-asset sensitivity tier (`public` / `team` / `restricted` / `embargo`). Restricted and embargo assets are **server-baked blurred** in browse views — the blur is a real preview variant so even a network-tap leak is blurred. A `Reveal` button lifts the blur for the session and logs the reveal. Pairs with a generic scheduled-action engine (`change_sensitivity`, `restrict`, `delete`, `change_state`, `notify` actions on assets / posts / collections / users at a future timestamp), executed via the existing job queue. Common recipes: NDA expiry on a contractor auto-restricts every asset they uploaded; embargo → public flips at a marketing-supplied timestamp; trash auto-purges at 30 days. See ADR 0020.

items.title: Storage tooling
items.description: Storage usage dashboard, orphan cleanup, checksum verification, dedupe UI, bulk re-import, backup + restore, database tools. Extended with: scheduled integrity checks with off-peak windows, tiered storage / offline archive (S3 Glacier / tape with fetch-on-demand surfaces), per-download bandwidth tracking attributed to teams + users.

items.title: Reports & analytics
items.description: Asset usage, user activity, storage trends, job performance, custom dashboards, scheduled reports, drafts, trash, activity log surfaces. Extended with: custom SQL report builder with placeholder variables (date range / team / user), CSV / Excel / PDF export per report, server-rendered report thumbnails, per-collection download analytics, scheduled email delivery of any report on a cron expression.

items.title: Community & moderation
items.description: Reports queue, comment moderation, banned users / IPs, anonymous browse policy, rate limits, bookmarks. Extended with: comment flagging with reason tracking, email escalation to admins on flagged content, per-comment hide / restore with audit trail, activity stream surfaced as a structured comments thread (`barts_log_to_comments` pattern), structured support intake — `/contact` form with categorization (bug / feature / abuse / account help / other) feeds into the same moderation queue with assignment, status tracking, and SLA timers; replaces the loose `email the admin` pattern with a queryable surface, and a personal activity feed on the user dashboard surfacing followed posts, recently viewed assets, bookmarks, pending notifications, and the user's own recent uploads + comments — pulled from the audit log (Phase 1.40) filtered to the user's visibility scope.

items.title: Announcements home widget
items.description: Operator-authored announcements with audience scoping (`org` / `team:{name}` / `role:{name}`), severity tiers (info / notice / warning / critical), optional schedule (`nbf` / `exp`), pinning, and per-user read state. Homepage hero strip shows the top three active for the user; account dashboard tile shows the full list with read state. Auto-fed from system events — planned maintenance, license upgrade, failed scheduled jobs, federation peer offline — become announcements automatically. Chat platforms (Phase 1.30) mirror new announcements to the configured Slack channel. See ADR 0029.

items.title: Chat platform integrations
items.description: Slack first, then Teams + Discord via the same provider abstraction. Outbound: rich Block-Kit-style messages for every notifiable event with deep-link buttons back into the post-detail modal. Inbound: `/aa search <query>`, `/aa post <id>`, `/aa upload` slash commands. Unfurl: Artist Alley URLs in chat get rich previews with blur respect for sensitive content. DM notifications opt-in via per-user Slack account connect. Admin surface defines per-event channel routing rules (`event:upload.completed in team:Concept Art → #concept-art-feed`). Chat is a delivery channel within the existing notification-rule subsystem from Phase 1.18 — not a separate engine. See ADR 0022.

items.title: External platform integrations
items.description: Provider-abstraction layer for outbound publishing and inbound asset ingestion against Vimeo, YouTube, Adobe Creative Cloud Libraries, and Falcon.io. Each provider is a Go package in `app/internal/platforms/<name>/` implementing a common interface (publish / pull / sync / embed / webhook). Linked-asset model stores `platform_links[]` on the resource row so the post-detail modal shows `Published to Vimeo (in sync)` and flags drift / deletion. Pull-as-asset uses the same `origin_*` row flag that federation does — the storage layer doesn't care whether content came from a peer AA or an external platform. OAuth client secrets in Cloudflare Worker Secrets; per-studio refresh tokens encrypted at rest. License tier caps concurrent platform connections via the tangled-derivation model. See ADR 0021.

items.title: RSS / Atom feeds
items.description: Standard syndication for collections, saved searches, user uploads, and tags so studios can wire Artist Alley into feed readers, Slack / Teams / Discord RSS connectors, and Zapier / n8n / Make / IFTTT triggers with no custom integration. URLs: `/feed/collection/{slug}.atom`, `/feed/search/{id}.atom`, `/feed/user/{handle}/uploads.atom`, `/feed/tag/{slug}.atom`. Atom primary, RSS 2.0 for compatibility. Per-user feed token in the URL for non-public content; revocable in account settings. Embargo + restricted items filter out of feeds entirely. Server-side cache 5 min with ETag + If-Modified-Since. See ADR 0023.

items.title: AI creative editing
items.description: Provider-abstracted in-paint, out-paint, variations, and remove-background tools in the asset viewer's Creative tools panel. Backed by the **capability add-on layer** from Phase 1.42 (ADR 0034) — the `image-inpaint` and `image-generation` capability slots resolve to whichever add-on the operator installed: locally-hosted **ComfyUI / Stable Diffusion / Flux add-ons** (open to every tier; operator brings the GPU) OR cloud-bridged **OpenAI / Stability AI add-ons** (Pro+ for the cloud bridge, with token budgets). Generated images are new assets that share a `creative_lineage` relationship with the source — the source is never overwritten. The new asset's metadata records add-on, version, prompt, seed, and parameters for both licensing and audit. Bring-your-own API keys at Enterprise; metered cloud-bridge at Pro. See ADR 0026 + ADR 0034.

items.title: Featured collections & homepage curation
items.description: Tree edges on the collection model (`collection_parent_id`, capped at depth 5) + a `featured` boolean with `team` / `org` / `public` scope. The same tree powers the team dashboard, the global signed-in homepage, and the anonymous public landing — one model, three audiences. Each featured node has an optional `hero_asset_id` (the card cover) and a `featured_order` integer for sibling sort. Cascade-publish flips a parent + children at once. Public featured collections respect per-asset sensitivity from ADR 0020 — an `embargo` asset shows only its title until embargo lifts. See ADR 0027.

items.title: Brand workspace
items.description: Curated overlay on the collection + theme model: a `brand_kit` binds a set of canonical collections, an editable design-token export (CSS / Tailwind / JSON / Figma tokens v3), a markdown guidelines doc with inline asset blocks, per-asset usage rules (`internal-only` / `partner` / `press` / `public`), and a publish state. Public portal at `/brand/{slug}`. Token export at `/brand/{slug}/tokens.json` for automated pipelines. Brand-steward role is Pro+; everyone can read. Usage rules enforced through the Phase 1.18 conditional download terms. See ADR 0025.

items.title: PBR 3D viewer polish
items.description: Right-side inspector in `ModelView.svelte` review mode: per-material list with hide / solo toggles, editable live PBR params (base color, metallic, roughness, normal strength, emissive) with the source asset never written, per-map texture preview that hand-offs to the texture inspector (Phase 1.18.B-16), curated 8-pack of IBL HDR environments + a project-HDR picker, A / B wipe between two materials on the same mesh (reusing the 1.18.B-8 A/B compare primitives). Override sets export as a structured `material_review.json` attached to the post — engineers ingesting reviews don't have to parse prose. See ADR 0028.

items.title: Federation
items.description: Peer servers, inbound + outbound feeds, sync status, conflict resolution. The data model already carries `origin_server_id` so today's single-instance code is forward-compatible.

items.title: Plugin ecosystem
items.description: WASM extension model via Extism. In-tree Go packages until external authors arrive.

items.title: Operator-configurable ad slots
items.description: Opt-in surface for operators running public-facing community instances (fan sites, festival hubs, art-school portfolios) to monetize hosting via ads. Defined zones across feed top / between-every-Nth feed item / sidebar top + bottom / post-modal sidebar / footer; each zone is toggled and provider-bound per instance. Providers ship for Google AdSense, Meta Audience Network, Carbon Ads, EthicalAds, and a custom-HTML option. Default off everywhere; AAA-internal studios see zero ad markup. Operator allow-lists categories (block gambling / adult / political / whatever) + sets frequency rules. Privacy compliance: ad slots auto-enable the third-party-embeds category in the cookie banner (ADR 0024) and do NOT load until consent. Per-user opt-out in account settings; Pro / Enterprise tiers may auto-suppress ads for paid users at the operator's option. No revenue share — operator ad income is theirs. No anti-AdBlock measures. Ad slots are sandboxed iframes with reserved dimensions to avoid CLS. **Distribution: premium add-on** (`aa-ads`) per ADR 0038 — the admin Ad Slots surface is in core but shows an `Install aa-ads to enable` empty state until the add-on is licensed; payment / serving / consent-routing code paths live in the proprietary add-on artifact. Available to all license tiers; orthogonal to Community / Pro / Enterprise. See ADR 0030 + ADR 0038.

items.title: Commerce — Stripe + Shopify
items.description: Operator-side commerce for selling content directly: digital downloads (concept-art packs, asset bundles, soundtracks), print-on-demand merchandise, physical originals, subscription access to WIP / patron tiers. Provider-abstracted with Stripe (digital + physical + subscription), Shopify (full storefront for physical + tax + shipping), Gumroad (lightweight digital + subscription) at launch. Listings attach to assets / posts / collections / brand-kit items with pricing, delivery type, license-grant clause. Digital fulfillment reuses Phase 1.26 share links — buyer gets a single-use signed link with 90-day expiry after payment. Subscription access expires via the Phase 1.28 scheduled-action engine. Tax + refunds + disputes defer to the payment processor. Active-listing caps (Community 5, Pro 500, Enterprise unlimited + organization-level Stripe / Shopify accounts) stack on top of the add-on subscription. Per-instance public storefront at `/shop/{slug}`. No revenue share on operator sales — operator's bank gets the proceeds. Federated peers can surface remote listings read-only with a `buy on origin` CTA. **Distribution: premium add-on** (`aa-commerce`) per ADR 0038 — the admin Commerce surface and storefront route are in core but show an `Install aa-commerce to enable` empty state until licensed; payment processing, webhook signing, storefront rendering, and license-grant emission live in the proprietary add-on. The add-on subscription is the lever for monetizing operators who themselves monetize via the platform; tier caps are orthogonal. See ADR 0031 + ADR 0038.

items.title: Public demo — ephemeral per-visitor sandboxes
items.description: Public demo at `demo.artist-alley.org` that provisions a personal, isolated Artist Alley instance per visitor on demand, pre-seeded with curated CC0 + public-domain sample art (Blender Demo Files / Kenney / Open Game Art / Met Museum / NASA media / Sintel / Project Gutenberg), auto-destroyed after a 60-minute wall-clock TTL or 30-minute idle timeout. Each sandbox is a full Artist Alley binary running with `DEMO_MODE=true` — federation disabled (no peer pairing accepted, no outbound activities), SMTP disabled, license validation skipped, premium add-on surfaces show 'available in self-host' empty states, storage capped at 1 GB / 200 assets per sandbox. Visitor is logged in as an admin with full capabilities so they can poke the upload pipeline, review canvas, universal viewer, admin shell, and theme system end to end. **Zero cross-visitor moderation surface by construction**: each sandbox is its own isolated VM; nothing visitors upload ever reaches any other visitor or any other Artist Alley instance. Email signup with magic-link verification is required up front (filters drive-by spam and hit-and-run abuse, captures marketing-funnel contact at moment of highest intent, lets us rate-limit per email rather than per IP). The same magic link doubles as the 7-day extension link — no second signup. Marketing-list opt-in is a separate checkbox per ADR 0024 privacy posture. Provisioner is a separate ~500-1000 LOC Go service in `mscrnt/aa-demo-provisioner` (public repo) that handles Cloudflare Turnstile gating, Fly.io Machines API integration, per-IP and global rate limits, budget-cap enforcement (~$250/mo default ceiling), and the destroy cron. Hosting: Fly.io Machines auto-stopping on idle for compute, R2 for the seed pack, Cloudflare for DNS + Turnstile. Realistic launch cost ~$10-20/month at 200 sandbox creations / mo; scales linearly to ~$100-150/mo at 10k creations / mo with a hard ceiling at the budget cap. Sub-phases: 1.48.A demo-mode binary flag + integration tests; 1.48.B seed-pack loader (downloads + extracts + ingests on boot); 1.48.C sandbox quotas at the handler layer; 1.48.D provisioner repo + Fly.io integration + Turnstile + rate limits + budget cap + destroy cron + claim-via-email flow; 1.48.E seed-pack curation + assembly + R2 upload; 1.48.F landing-page copy + funnel + 60-second teaser video; 1.48.G operational runbook. See ADR 0045.

items.title: Native viewers for proprietary DCC formats
items.description: Inventory + thumbnail + interactive in-browser viewing for proprietary DCC scene files (`.max`, `.mb`, `.ma`, and follow-on formats — `.hip`, `.zpr`, `.spp`) that today have no first-class home anywhere outside their authoring DCC. The architecture splits across three deliberate layers — two free, one premium — so the AGPL core gives immediate value without exposing the proprietary work. **Layer 1 (free, in-tree): `dcc-fileinfo` Go metadata reader.** Parses the OLE2 / CFBF container of `.max` files via the open Microsoft spec; enumerates `FileAssetMetaData2/3`, `SummaryInformation`, `DllDirectory` streams; lists texture / XRef references, embedded thumbnail (if present), plugin manifest, modified-by-user, last-saved-version. No chunk semantics, no GPL exposure — CFBF container is public, asset-metadata streams are documented by Autodesk in KB articles. `.ma` (ASCII MEL) parses as a tokenizer. `.mb` (binary IFF) parses via the documented chunked structure. Powers the upload-time "what's in this file?" answer without paying Blender's cold-boot cost. **Layer 2 (free, in-tree): Blender worker pipeline for thumbnails + conversion.** Existing Phase 1.18 thumbnail-worker pattern, extended to `.max` via `nrgsille76/io_scene_max` (Blender 4.2+ extension, GPL-2.0+), to `.ma` via Blender's MEL-bridge add-ons, and to `.mb` deferred until paid-customer demand. The worker is a subprocess from the Go core; GPL stays inside the Blender container. Output is glTF / USD / a rendered preview — universal, fork-safe, no contamination of the AGPL core or of premium add-ons. **Layer 3 (premium add-on `aa-dcc-viewer`, ADR 0038): the interactive live viewer + proprietary routing algorithm.** Native parser for the common-case scene shape (geometry / transforms / basic materials / cameras / lights) gives instant interactive scrubbing without a Blender round-trip; the proprietary part is the routing intelligence + chunk-ID heuristic database that decides per-chunk whether to handle natively or fall back to the cached Blender-glTF for that chunk. Web-optimised intermediate streaming format. Material translation layer (V-Ray / Corona / Arch & Design → glTF PBR). Closed-source artifact, EULA-licensed, Ed25519 `.lic`-gated per ADR 0038. **Clean-room posture is load-bearing**: no GPL-licensed reverse-engineered code lands in `aa-dcc-viewer`. The Kaetemi blog series + Autodesk public KB are the spec; existing GPL implementations (`io_scene_max`, `Importer3D`) are read for what they document, never lifted from. Sub-phases: 1.47.A `dcc-fileinfo` metadata reader (free, in-tree); 1.47.B Blender worker extension for `.max` + `.ma` (free, in-tree, extends Phase 1.18 thumbnail pipeline); 1.47.C `aa-dcc-viewer` premium add-on with native parser + routing algorithm + material translation (paid, proprietary); 1.47.D extended format coverage (`.hip` / `.spp` / `.zpr`, demand-driven; same three-layer pattern). See ADR 0039 + ADR 0038.

items.title: Premium DCC integrations
items.description: First-party plugins for commercial DCCs that push assets, scene thumbnails, and version-up workflows from inside the artist's tool of choice — Maya, 3ds Max, Houdini, ZBrush, Substance Painter, Substance Designer, Marvelous Designer, Marmoset Toolbag, Unity, Unreal. Plugins live in their respective DCCs' native plugin systems (Maya scripted-plugin + MEL/Python panel, ZScript for ZBrush, HDA + Python panel for Houdini, etc.) and talk to a stable HTTP/WebSocket contract on the AA side that any DCC plugin can target. **Distribution: premium add-ons** per ADR 0038 — one paid add-on per DCC (`aa-maya`, `aa-3dsmax`, `aa-zbrush`, `aa-houdini`, `aa-substance`, `aa-marvelous`, `aa-marmoset`, `aa-unity`, `aa-unreal`). Pricing is per-seat per-year, matching DCC vendor conventions. **Free DCC integrations stay free** — Blender add-on, Krita / Inkscape / GIMP / FreeCAD ship as in-tree integrations under the AGPL core, no license required, because the open-source DCC ecosystem is foundational to the audience and we don't paywall artists who use free tools. v1 ships Maya + Substance Painter + Unreal (broadest game-studio reach); subsequent DCCs follow demand. Plugin auto-update channels live on the same Cloudflare-Pages-hosted registry as the capability add-on registry from Phase 1.42. See ADR 0038.

items.title: Cloud-bridge add-ons (AI / translation / transcription)
items.description: Operator-pays-us-metered alternative to running local AI add-ons — for studios who don't want to provision GPU infrastructure but want to use Phase 1.42 capability slots (image-embedding / transcription / OCR / image-generation / image-inpaint) and Phase 1.44 translation. We host the inference on Cloudflare Workers AI / a managed inference backend; the operator's instance calls our cloud-bridge endpoint, signed with their Ed25519 `.lic` (ADR 0017), and we bill per token / per minute / per image with monthly statements. **Distribution: premium add-ons** per ADR 0038 — `aa-cloud-ai` (OpenAI / Anthropic / Stability bridge for image-generation + inpaint slots), `aa-cloud-translation` (DeepL / OpenAI bridge for the Phase 1.44 text-translation slot), `aa-cloud-transcription` (managed Whisper for the transcription slot). **Locally-hosted equivalents always remain free** — `ai-clip`, `ai-whisper`, `ai-tesseract` (Phase 1.42) and a future `ai-translation` local add-on stay free under the curated registry. The cloud bridge is opt-in operational convenience, not a GPU-gating end-run. Air-gapped operators are unaffected — they pick the local add-ons. Per-add-on usage caps + budgets in `/admin/billing`; operators set their own ceilings. See ADR 0038 + ADR 0034 + ADR 0017.

items.title: Caption & subtitle artifacts
items.description: Caption and subtitle tracks as first-class artifacts on audio / video assets — produced by the Whisper transcription add-on (Phase 1.42 / ADR 0034), edited by humans through a timeline + cue-list UI, stored as canonical WebVTT, served on-the-fly as VTT / SRT / TTML / IMSC, and auto-attached to every distribution channel (viewer, share link, download bundle, commerce delivery, federation peer, RSS enclosure). Three-state lifecycle (raw → draft → final → archived) and explicit producer attribution (`ai-whisper` / `ai-translation` / `manual` / `imported` / `derived`) protect users from shipping unreviewed AI output to viewers. Multi-language native — one track per language per asset, no schema gymnastics. Translation is a second AI hop via a new `text-translation` capability slot (satisfied by future add-ons — OpenAI / Anthropic / DeepL / Argos local), always landing as `raw` for human review. Editor lives in the asset viewer right-rail with waveform + cue list + cue editor + Aegisub-shaped keyboard shortcuts (Enter = next, Ctrl-K = split, Ctrl-M = merge). External imports (ADR 0036) recognise sidecar `.srt` / `.vtt` / `.ass` files and attach them as caption tracks instead of orphan text assets. Phase 1.18.B-3 is the viewer-side consumer; this phase owns production + editing + serving + reuse. Sub-phases: 1.44.A data model + auto-caption pipeline + serving + viewer attachment (raw → served, no editor); 1.44.B editor (timeline + cue list + draft/final lifecycle + version history); 1.44.C translation slot + dispatcher + bilingual cue editor view; 1.44.D reuse hooks + extra formats (download bundles, share links, commerce bundles, TTML/IMSC, import-connector sidecar attachment); 1.44.E (deferred) burn-in subtitle variants for delivery. See ADR 0037.

items.title: External imports framework
items.description: First-class subsystem for pulling assets out of external systems — network shares, S3 / R2 / B2 buckets, single HTTP archives, git / git LFS repos, Perforce depots, ShotGrid (Flow Production Tracking) sites, OneDrive / SharePoint document libraries, Google Drive team folders — through a single connector contract. Three primitives (Source / Run / Item) and a pluggable Connector interface in `internal/imports/` cover the entire matrix; the admin surface at `/admin/imports` ships the source list, per-source detail with mapping rules, run history, and a per-item review queue for conflicts. Two storage modes per source: `ingest` copies bytes into the Artist Alley filestore; `reference` leaves them on the source and dispatches reads through the connector (`import-ref` storage backend), trading storage cost against source-availability coupling — the operator picks per source. Lifecycle inherits the strong patterns of legacy filesystem-sync features (path-as-metadata via mapping rules, mtime / hash change detection, delete → archive → revive policy, per-source process lock) and fixes the common pain points on purpose: multi-source instead of one filesystem; UI-managed instead of `config.php`-only; explicit conflict policies (`source_wins` / `local_wins` / `review`) plus a user-edit-locked flag so source overwrites never trample a field a person changed by hand; per-item review queue with side-by-side diff for `review` resolutions; per-source attribution instead of one global importer user. Push support where the source offers it (Drive watch channels, Graph subscriptions, ShotGrid event log) cuts the every-hour-scan-the-tree pattern for sources that bleed money on it. Audit hooks fire `import.*` into Phase 1.40; metrics expose under `import_` prefix in Phase 1.41. Sub-phases: 1.43.A framework (data model + scheduler + admin surface + audit/metrics, no connectors), 1.43.B foundation connectors that share ~80% implementation (fs / s3 / http / git), 1.43.C ShotGrid, 1.43.D Perforce, 1.43.E Microsoft 365 (OneDrive + SharePoint via Graph), 1.43.F Google Drive. Order of C / D / E / F is demand-driven. See ADR 0036.

sections.title: Things we deliberately aren't building
sections.summary: Scope boundaries, made explicit so we hold the line.

items.title: A general-purpose DAM
items.description: We're shaped specifically for studio art-review workflows.

items.title: A pipeline integration platform
items.description: We're a destination for finished and in-progress art, not a Perforce / Shotgrid replacement.

items.title: A hosted-only SaaS product
items.description: Self-hostable by design. A managed hosted Pro offering is on the table for indie studios without IT capacity, but the product remains fully self-hostable, and Enterprise customers always self-host.

items.title: NFTs, crypto-payment rails, or blockchain anything
items.description: Different audience, polluting brand, opens reputational risk around rugpull-adjacent projects. Operators who want crypto can build it as a third-party plugin once the WASM plugin ecosystem (Phase 1.23) lands; we will not ship one.

items.title: Pulling features into paywalls retroactively
items.description: Features promised at a given license tier do not move out of it. Premium add-ons (ADR 0038) are an orthogonal axis on top of the Community / Pro / Enterprise tiers — they add capabilities operators use to monetize third parties or that carry operational burden we operate on their behalf. They never reach back into features the tier already includes.
